title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

The happy-path default (a diff with no backtick runs keeping the conventional 3-backtick fence) is exercised only indirectly by sibling tests; an explicit assertion that longestBacktickRun=0 yields a length-3 fence would lock the max(3, ...) floor directly.

title: The composite-promote test promotes both pen entries, so it never exercises byt…

title: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Sit…
body: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Site A lines ~341-343, Site B AC4 ~line 745), so they execute while process.stderr.write is still patched. On assertion failure the framework's diff output routes into the captured chunks rather than the real terminal, which can obscure failure diagnostics. Consider exposing the captured chunks after the helper returns (or asserting outside the callback) so failures print normally. Non-blocking: restore is guaranteed by the finally, and all tests pass.

title: The self-pid write is placed before runContainerEnsureGuard's early-return, so …

This mirrors the existing writeSessionStartFn placement and matches the spec, so it is not a defect; a future note could clarify whether the container path wants its own liveness marker.

Bumping its prd to storyCount 2 would restore the branch it intends to verify. Non-blocking: the assertion (zero notify/events) still holds.

title: runPause always returns 0 even if setPause silently swallowed a write failure (…
body: runPause always returns 0 even if setPause silently swallowed a write failure (permission error), so a pause that never actually wrote the marker is indistinguishable from success. Consider having setPause surface a best-effort boolean so pause can warn (not fail) when the marker could not be written. (Carried from review round 1; non-blocking.)

title: sendBareSubmitKey presses Enter into a pane the idle gate observed as BUSY, up …
body: sendBareSubmitKey presses Enter into a pane the idle gate observed as BUSY, up to maxAttempts-1 times per push. The module header's duplication-safety argument (no payload text is re-sent) and its 'Residue NOT closed' paragraph (lines 54-58) cover the prompt-glyph forgery residue but not this one: a bare Enter is also a confirmation keypress, so a half-typed operator line, or any modal/selection row the TUI happens to be rendering (which by construction never starts with the prompt glyph and therefore always reads 'not delivered', guaranteeing the remediation fires), gets submitted or accepted. State this residue explicitly alongside the existing one. Carried unchanged from round 2.

The accommodation is legitimate and the tmux docs confirm `-S -` starts at the beginning of history, but the test's original claim ('lands in the orchestrator pane capture-pane output') is now weaker: it proves the line entered pane HISTORY, not that it is on screen. Either say so in the header comment or boot a taller pane so the visible-screen assertion survives. Carried unchanged from round 2.

Derive the expected count (maxAttempts settles + maxAttempts-1 backoffs) instead.

It appears to exist only to mirror the AC's literal 'submitRemediations >= 1' wording. Drop it and let the exact toEqual carry the criterion.

The existing entry did not become false (it says 'exhausts its retries without confirming submission', which post-fix is now true on BOTH reasons rather than just one), and the glossary is selective rather than an exhaustive event catalog, so this is not a doc-drift defect. Still worth a one-line entry per the Knowledge-Layer Routing table, since push-recovered is exactly the kind of bounded-context vocabulary that channel exists for. Related pre-existing staleness, out of scope for this diff: the 'composer-emptied state check' entry at line 182 still describes the pre-CAM-359/CAM-364 verification mechanism.

title: Unchanged from round 1: this test's only assertion is `expect(helpCall).toBeDef…

The probe's own branches are now genuinely covered (test/commands/run-effort-preflight.test.ts), so this is no longer a coverage hole, but since the fake returns empty stdout the probe must answer false: adding `expect(dispatchedCmd).not.toContain('--effort')` would make this test verify the production default's real effect on the dispatched argv.

title: The spawn-resolution event is emitted BEFORE the stdout JSON line is written, s…
body: The spawn-resolution event is emitted BEFORE the stdout JSON line is written, so a failing event append (permissions, full disk) throws and discards an otherwise successful resolution, degrading the wrapper to the fallback path for observability reasons alone. Writing the JSON line first, then emitting the event, keeps the primary contract independent of the audit side effect.

title: The emitted event stamps `uuid: 'orch-resolve'` (a literal) while the bash fall…
body: The emitted event stamps `uuid: 'orch-resolve'` (a literal) while the bash fallback event in the same log stamps the real respawn uuid ("$sid"). The wrapper writes the fresh uuid to .cam-orch-session immediately before invoking the resolver, so orch-resolve could read that marker and stamp the real session id, making per-session attribution consistent across both emitters of this loop's events.

title: The top-level `cam help` internal-commands section lists sidecar, orch-recycle-…
body: The top-level `cam help` internal-commands section lists sidecar, orch-recycle-watch, sidecar-liveness-watch and orch-budget, but not orch-resolve; ORCH_RESOLVE_HELP explicitly states it is not listed. That is self-consistent, but it breaks the established pattern that every `cam run`-spawned internal command is discoverable there, which matters now that operators will see orch-resolve in the pane command and in the event log.

title: Repeat of two round-1 suggestions still open: (a) the wrapper parses only .mode…
body: Repeat of two round-1 suggestions still open: (a) the wrapper parses only .model and .effort and ignores the .backend the resolver prints, so a mid-session backend switch to codex would feed a codex slug to the hardcoded `claude --model` (same mismatch already exists on main at the initial spawn, so not a regression, but live re-resolution makes it reachable mid-session); (b) readPhaseEffort returns any non-empty string, so `efforts.orchestrator = 'maximum'` flows into --effort and into the audit event (claude 2.1.220 only warns and falls back, per the official CLI reference tier set low|medium|high|xhigh|max), recording a tier claude never applied.

Still, buildOrchestratorPaneCommand is now a ~90-line bash-template builder with its own test block and remains the natural next extraction (run-auth-preflight.ts / run-effort-preflight.ts precedent) rather than a fourth ceiling raise next cycle.

title: The module header justifies positive-signal-only detection by saying a future b…
body: The module header justifies positive-signal-only detection by saying a future bunfs prefix change 'degrades to orch-resolve's loud fail-safe fallback ... rather than propagating a silent dead-child failure'. That rationale is true only for the run.ts call site: the primitive's second consumer, forkMonitor (src/retry/launcher.ts:242), has no fallback and no post-spawn liveness check, so a prefix change there would silently re-kill the retry-monitor child, i.e. exactly the bug this branch fixes. The real repo-wide guard is the new US-003 compiled integration test (which fails loudly in CI on a prefix change); the comment would be more accurate naming that pin instead of a fallback the forkMonitor path does not have.

title: The header comment states "stdin: 'ignore' is required on every spawnSync here …
body: The header comment states "stdin: 'ignore' is required on every spawnSync here (both the outer build/run calls and the fixture's own inner self-spawn)", but the build spawnSync at line 154 does not pass stdin and the test is green. Either the comment overstates the requirement or the build call is missing it; as written the comment is a claim the code disproves, which is the exact comment-vs-runtime drift class this repo has been burned by before.

title: Carried over from review round 1 and still unaddressed: both monkeypatched test…
body: Carried over from review round 1 and still unaddressed: both monkeypatched tests restore process.execPath / process.argv[1] with plain statements after the forkMonitor(...) call rather than in a try/finally. Assertions run after the restore so an assertion failure is safe, but a throw inside forkMonitor would leak a bogus global process.execPath into every later test in the same runner process. A small withPatchedArgv(...) helper shared by both tests would make the restore unconditional.
